_comment: Everything in this funnel that is a setting rather than copy. Copy is in copy.json (word for word from the IT board v56). The form and its validation are in core.mjs, the routing rules in route.mjs. Read g/uk-it-growth/LAUNCH.md before changing anything here.
_path: The address the funnel is served at. The build checks it against the redirect and header rules in netlify.toml. Landing page and five outcome pages sit directly under it.
_origin: One host for the whole chain. sessionStorage (the consent choice, the fire-once guard) is per origin, so the ad URL, the form, the booking page and the Calendly forward must all use this one.
_live: While false the build stays green with items missing and the lead function answers every submission with a 503 and stores nothing. Set true only when the build says nothing is outstanding. The build then refuses to finish while calendlyUrl is empty.

links._comment: The pages built from legal.json. The older /lp/privacy/ and /lp/terms/ belong to the legacy /lp funnel and stay as they are.

legal._registerCheck: Whether the privacy notice and the terms say that the company is checked against Companies House. Set true in the same change that sets COMPANIES_HOUSE_API_KEY in production, then build; the notice must never describe a check that is not made. The words themselves are in legal.json, in the blocks and rows marked "when": "register".

funnel._qualifiedEvent: A custom event, never the standard Lead. Fires on /book and /review only, with eventID = lead_id, and only after the visitor has accepted. The server sends the same event with the same id (Conversions API), so Meta counts it once.
funnel._calendlyUrl: The event URL with no query string, from Calendly: Share, Add to website, Inline embed. Empty is allowed only while live is false. The booking page adds name, email and utm parameters itself, with lead_id in utm_content. Calendly's own redirect after booking must stay off: the page forwards to /takk itself.
funnel._calendlyLeadParam: The tracking parameter that carries the lead id into Calendly, where the Calendly Zap reads it back (Invitee Created, tracking). Calendly passes on only utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_content and utm_term. It replaces the value of the same name, so the ad's own value stays on the application. Change it here and in the Zap together, never in one place.

clickup._comment: The ClickUp list the daily reconciliation compares against: IT - UK - Commision. Leads carry tag growth-2m in it. The custom field lead_id on that list holds the key.
